issue_title: Log a structured warning when a widget import row is skipped
issue_body:
The CSV importer silently skips malformed rows, so operators cannot tell why an import produced fewer widgets than the file had rows.

When a row is skipped, log a structured warning at WARN level with `event=skipped_row`, the 1-based `line` number, and a `reason`. At the end of the import, log the total skipped count.

plan.summary: Log a structured WARN for each skipped import row and a final skipped-row total.

approach.description: In the row loop of internal/importer/csv.go, on a parse failure log WARN event=skipped_row with line and reason.
Count skipped rows and log an INFO summary with skipped=<n> when the import finishes.

verification.test_strategy: csv_test.go captures log output with a test handler: a file with two malformed rows yields two skipped_row warnings carrying lines 3 and 7, and a summary with skipped=2.
verification.rollback_plan: Revert the PR. The change is additive; no data migration needs reversing.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Importing a CSV whose line 3 is malformed logs one WARN record with event=skipped_row, line=3 and a non-empty reason.
Importing a CSV with two malformed rows logs a final summary carrying skipped=2.
The importer either logs a warning for a skipped row or does not log one.

risks_and_assumptions: The logger already supports structured attributes.

catching_examples.note: ac-import-log-or-not is vacuously true: 'either logs or does not log' holds for every implementation.
One criterion is a tautology that can never fail; replace it with one that fails when no warning is logged.

non_catching_examples.note: No test covers a file whose header row itself is malformed.
The summary log line could also report the number of widgets created.
A very large file with many bad rows will produce one WARN per row; consider the log volume.
No test asserts the importer logs a warning for a skipped row when the reason is empty.
Logging behaviour should be specified in the importer README, including event=skipped_row.
